segments.arabic: [1239] حدثنا بشر بن الحكم حدثنا سفيان بن عيينة أخبرنا إسحاق بن عبد الله بن أبي طلحة أنه سمع أنس بن مالك رضى الله تعالى عنه يقول
segments.english: Bishr ibn al-Hakam related to us: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah related to us: Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah informed us that he heard Anas ibn Malik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, say:

segments.arabic: اشتكى بن لأبي طلحة قال: فمات وأبو طلحة خارج فلما رأت امرأته أنه قد مات هيأت شيئا ونحته في جانب البيت فلما جاء أبو طلحة قال كيف الغلام قالت قد هدأت نفسه وأرجو أن يكون قد استراح وظن أبو طلحة أنها صادقة قال: فبات فلما أصبح اغتسل فلما أراد أن يخرج أعلمته أنه قد مات فصلى مع النبي ﷺ ثم أخبر النبي ﷺ بما كان منهما، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: لعل الله أن يبارك لكما في ليلتكما
segments.english: A son of Abu Talhah fell ill. He said: He died while Abu Talhah was away. When his wife saw that he had died, she prepared something and moved him to the side of the house. When Abu Talhah came, he asked, “How is the boy?” She said, “His soul has become still, and I hope he has found rest.” Abu Talhah thought that she was telling the truth. He said: He spent the night. When morning came, he bathed. When he intended to leave, she informed him that the boy had died. He prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then informed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, of what had happened between them. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Perhaps Allah will bless you both in your night.”

segments.arabic: قال سفيان، فقال رجل من الأنصار فرأيت لهما تسعة أولاد كلهم قد قرأ القرآن
segments.english: Sufyan said: A man of the Ansar then said, “I saw that they had nine children, all of whom had recited the Qur’an.”

comparisons.note: Renders فرأيت as I think rather than preserving its seeing/reporting form. The original locator also captured the following differently punctuated chapter heading and its context; the revised locator separates that material.

checkedBody: Narrated Anas bin Malik:

One of the sons of Abu Talha became sick and died and Abu Talha at that time was not at home. When his wife saw that he was dead, she prepared him (washed and shrouded him) and placed him somewhere in the house. When Abu Talha came, he asked, "How is the boy?" She said, "The child is quiet and I hope he is in peace." Abu Talha thought that she had spoken the truth. Abu Talha passed the night and in the morning took a bath and when he intended to go out, she told him that his son had died, Abu Talha offered the (morning) prayer with the Prophet and informed the Prophet of what happened to them. Allah's Apostle said, "May Allah bless you concerning your night. (That is, may Allah bless you with good offspring)." Sufyan said, "One of the Ansar said, 'They (i.e. Abu Talha and his wife) had nine sons and all of them became reciters of the Quran (by heart).' "
comparisons.note: Adds washing/shrouding, morning, offspring and memorization explanations; changes the selected لعل صيغة and omits the closing seeing/reporting form.

notes: The next web heading uses XLI. CHAPTER: instead of the usual Roman-numeral colon. Separate that chapter context from the report body before comparing or hashing it.

Preserve the unspecified prepared-something, stillness, hope, both-person address and actual I-saw in the closing. No washing, shrouding, intercourse, grandchildren, memorization or named speaker is inserted. The digital بن spelling is retained unchanged; the English conveys son.

segments.arabic: [1241] حدثنا الحسن بن عبد العزيز حدثنا يحيى بن حسان حدثنا قريش هو ابن حيان عن ثابت عن أنس بن مالك رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Al-Hasan ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related to us: Yahya ibn Hassan related to us: Quraysh—he is Ibn Hayyan—related to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: دخلنا مع رسول الله ﷺ على أبي سيف القين وكان ظئرا لإبراهيم عليه السلام فأخذ رسول الله ﷺ إبراهيم فقبله وشمه ثم دخلنا عليه بعد ذلك وإبراهيم يجود بنفسه فجعلت عينا رسول الله ﷺ تذرفان، فقال له عبد الرحمن بن عوف رضى الله تعالى عنه وأنت يا رسول الله، فقال: يا ابن عوف إنها رحمة ثم أتبعها بأخرى، فقال ﷺ إن العين تدمع والقلب يحزن ولا نقول إلا ما يرضى ربنا وإنا بفراقك يا إبراهيم لمحزونون
segments.english: We entered with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, upon Abu Sayf the blacksmith, who was the foster father of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took Ibrahim, kissed him and smelled him. Then we entered upon him after that, while Ibrahim was breathing his last. The eyes of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, began to shed tears. ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said to him, “Even you, Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Ibn ‘Awf, this is mercy.” Then he followed it with another, and said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “The eye sheds tears and the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord. And we are indeed grieved by your departure, Ibrahim.”

segments.arabic: رواه موسى عن سليمان بن المغيرة عن ثابت عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Musa narrated it from Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

comparisons.note: Calls Abu Sayf the father of Ibrahim’s wet-nurse, while the Khan comparison calls him her husband. The selected ظئرا needs explicit lexical review. The closing route omits Musa and Thabit, and the original locator includes the following unpunctuated chapter heading; the revised locator separates it. Classical commentary identifies ظئر as foster father, the husband of the wet-nurse, not her father. It also records another tear or another utterance for ثم أتبعها بأخرى; this working translation leaves the unspecified noun unfilled.

checkedBody: Narrated Anas bin Malik:

We went with Allah's Apostle (p.b.u.h) to the blacksmith Abu Saif, and he was the husband of the wet-nurse of Ibrahim (the son of the Prophet). Allah's Apostle took Ibrahim and kissed him and smelled him and later we entered Abu Saif's house and at that time Ibrahim was in his last breaths, and the eyes of Allah's Apostle (p.b.u.h) started shedding tears. 'Abdur Rahman bin 'Auf said, "O Allah's Apostle, even you are weeping!" He said, "O Ibn 'Auf, this is mercy." Then he wept more and said, "The eyes are shedding tears and the heart is grieved, and we will not say except what pleases our Lord, O Ibrahim ! Indeed we are grieved by your separation."
comparisons.note: Omits the full closing Musa/Sulayman/Thabit/Anas route and adds explanatory identification. The exact ظئر relationship needs lexical review. Do not supply weeping in the question or more tears in the unspecified then-he-followed-it-with-another phrase. Keep Ibrahim’s honorific, every Prophetic honorific and the complete closing route.

notes: Keep Ibrahim’s honorific, the complete closing corroborating route, and the lexical relationship review separate. The next web chapter heading is now excluded from this body.

Foster father follows the classical husband-of-wet-nurse explanation, not father-of-wet-nurse. Another is unspecified: commentary records a tear or utterance, so neither noun is inserted. Retain all five Prophetic honorifics, Ibrahim’s honorific and the complete Musa/Sulayman/Thabit/Anas closing route.

segments.arabic: [1242] حدثنا أصبغ عن ابن وهب قال: أخبرني عمرو عن سعيد بن الحارث الأنصارى عن عبد الله بن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Asbagh related to us, from Ibn Wahb, who said: ‘Amr informed me, from Sa‘id ibn al-Harith al-Ansari, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: اشتكى سعد بن عبادة شكوى له فأتاه النبي ﷺ يعوده مع عبد الرحمن بن عوف وسعد بن أبي وقاص وعبد الله بن مسعود رضى الله تعالى عنهم فلما دخل عليه فوجده في غاشية أهله، فقال قد قضى قالوا لا يا رسول الله فبكى النبي ﷺ فلما رأى القوم بكاء النبي ﷺ بكوا، فقال ألا تسمعون إن الله لا يعذب بدمع العين ولا بحزن القلب ولكن يعذب بهذا
segments.english: Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah fell ill with an illness of his. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to visit him with ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas and ‘Abd Allah ibn Mas‘ud, may Allah Most High be pleased with them. When he entered upon him and found him surrounded by his family, he asked, “Has he passed away?” They said, “No, Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wept. When the people saw the weeping of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, they wept. He said, “Do you not hear? Allah does not punish because of the eye’s tears or the heart’s grief, but He punishes because of this”—

segments.arabic: وأشار إلى لسانه
segments.english: and he pointed to his tongue—

segments.arabic: أو يرحم وإن الميت يعذب ببكاء أهله عليه
segments.english: “or shows mercy. And the deceased is indeed punished because of his family’s weeping over him.”

segments.arabic: وكان عمر رضي الله عنه يضرب فيه بالعصا ويرمي بالحجارة ويحثي بالتراب
segments.english: And ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to strike with a stick because of it, throw stones, and scatter dust.

comparisons.note: Contains the final Umar statement present in both prints but absent from the selected Arabic; it cannot be silently appended to this source translation.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Abdullah bin 'Umar :

Sad bin 'Ubada became sick and the Prophet along with 'Abdur Rahman bin 'Auf, Sad bin Abi Waqqas and 'Abdullah bin Masud visited him to enquire about his health. When he came to him, he found him surrounded by his household and he asked, "Has he died?" They said, "No, O Allah's Apostle." The Prophet wept and when the people saw the weeping of Allah's Apostle (p.b.u.h) they all wept. He said, "Will you listen? Allah does not punish for shedding tears, nor for the grief of the heart but he punishes or bestows His Mercy because of this." He pointed to his tongue and added, "The deceased is punished for the wailing of his relatives over him." 'Umar used to beat with a stick and throw stones and put dust over the faces (of those who used to wail over the dead).
comparisons.note: Contains the Umar closing statement absent from the selected Arabic and adds an explanatory parenthesis about the people concerned. The selected بكاء is weeping, not wailing. The printed supplement does not explicitly say faces or add an object identifying people who wail.

notes: Both Arabic prints and both English comparisons contain an Umar closing statement absent from the selected source. Record the omission; do not silently append it.

Retain the family-surrounding wording, all honorifics, the tongue gesture outside the speech and weeping rather than wailing. The separately labelled Umar note is connected through Ibn Umar according to Ibn Hajar, not part of the Prophet’s quoted words. No faces or object identifying wailers is added.

segments.arabic: [1243] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الله بن حوشب حدثنا عبد الوهاب حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد قال: أخبرتني عمرة قالت سمعت عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها تقول
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Hawshab related to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us; he said: ‘Amrah informed me; she said: I heard ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, say:

segments.arabic: لما جاء قتل زيد بن حارثة وجعفر وعبد الله بن رواحة جلس النبي ﷺ يعرف فيه الحزن وأنا أطلع من شق الباب فأتاه رجل، فقال: يا رسول الله إن نساء جعفر وذكر بكاءهن فأمره بأن ينهاهن فذهب الرجل ثم أتى، فقال قد نهيتهن وذكر أنهن لم يطعنه فأمره الثانية أن ينهاهن فذهب ثم أتى، فقال والله لقد غلبنني أو غلبننا
segments.english: When news of the killing of Zayd ibn Harithah, Ja‘far and ‘Abd Allah ibn Rawahah came, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sat down with grief apparent in him, while I was looking through the crack in the door. A man came to him and said, “Messenger of Allah, the women of Ja‘far”—and he mentioned their weeping. He ordered him to forbid them. The man went, then came and said, “I have forbidden them,” and mentioned that they had not obeyed him. He ordered him a second time to forbid them. He went, then came and said, “By Allah, they have indeed overcome me—or overcome us.”

segments.arabic: الشك من محمد بن حوشب
segments.english: The uncertainty is from Muhammad ibn Hawshab.

segments.arabic: فزعمت أن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: She stated that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: فاحث في أفواههن التراب فقلت: أرغم الله أنفك فوالله ما أنت بفاعل وما تركت رسول الله ﷺ من العناء
segments.english: “Then cast dust into their mouths.” I said, “May Allah rub your nose in the dust! By Allah, you are not going to do it, and you have not spared the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the trouble.”

comparisons.note: Drops Zayd ibn from Zayd ibn Harithah and omits the opening address to the Messenger. Preserve the named transmitter’s me/us uncertainty and every attribution. Keep the oath, future-facing you-are-not-going-to-do-it wording, all honorifics, and the separate Amrah/Aishah attribution without implying doubt.

checkedBody: Narrated Aisha:

When the news of the martyrdom of Zaid bin Haritha, Ja'far and 'Abdullah bin Rawaha came, the Prophet sat down looking sad, and I was looking through the chink of the door. A man came and said, "O Allah's Apostle! The women of Ja'far," and then he mentioned their crying . The Prophet (p.b.u.h) ordered h im to stop them from crying. The man went and came back and said, "I tried to stop them but they disobeyed." The Prophet (p.b.u.h) ordered him for the second time to forbid them. He went again and came back and said, "They did not listen to me, (or "us": the sub-narrator Muhammad bin Haushab is in doubt as to which is right). " ('Aisha added: The Prophet said, "Put dust in their mouths." I said (to that man), "May Allah stick your nose in the dust (i.e. humiliate you)." By Allah, you could not (stop the women from crying) to fulfill the order, besides you did not relieve Allah's Apostle from fatigue."

segments.arabic: [1244] حدثنا عبد الله بن عبد الوهاب حدثنا حماد بن زيد حدثنا أيوب عن محمد عن أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت

segments.arabic: أخذ علينا النبي ﷺ عند البيعة أن لا ننوح فما وفت منا امرأة غير خمس نسوة أم سليم وأم العلاء وابنة أبي سبرة امرأة معاذ وامرأتان أو ابنة أبي سبرة وامرأة معاذ وامرأة أخرى
segments.english: At the pledge of allegiance, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bound us not to wail. None of our women fulfilled it except five women: Umm Sulaym, Umm al-‘Ala’, the daughter of Abu Sabrah—Mu‘adh’s wife—and two women—or the daughter of Abu Sabrah and the wife of Mu‘adh and another woman.

comparisons.note: Its punctuation makes the daughter of Abu Sabrah and the wife of Muadh appear as separate people in the first list, losing the apposition. Both list alternatives need careful translation. The first list identifies the daughter of Abu Sabrah as Muadh’s wife; the second explicitly joins the two names with and. Both lists remain.

segments.arabic: [1245] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله حدثنا سفيان حدثنا الزهري عن سالم عن أبيه عن عامر بن ربيعة عن النبي ﷺ قال:

segments.arabic: إذا رأيتم الجنازة فقوموا حتى تخلفكم

segments.arabic: قال سفيان قال الزهري أخبرني سالم عن أبيه قال: أخبرنا عامر بن ربيعة عن النبي ﷺ زاد الحميدي حتى تخلفكم أو توضع
segments.english: Sufyan said: Al-Zuhri said: Salim informed me, from his father, who said: ‘Amir ibn Rabi‘ah informed us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Al-Humaydi added: “Until it leaves you behind or is put down.”

comparisons.note: Names Amr rather than Amir ibn Rabiah and abridges the second Zuhri/Salim route.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Amir bin Rabi'a:,
The Prophet said, "Whenever you see a funeral procession, stand up till the procession goes ahead of you." Al-Humaidi added, "Till the coffin leaves you behind or is put down."
comparisons.note: Omits Sufyan’s full second Zuhri/Salim route; preserve that transmission and the separately attributed al-Humaydi addition.

segments.arabic: [1246] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد حدثنا الليث عن نافع عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما عن عامر بن ربيعة رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ قال:

segments.arabic: إذا رأى أحدكم جنازة فإن لم يكن ماشيا معها فليقم حتى يخلفها أو تخلفه أو توضع من قبل أن تخلفه
segments.english: “When one of you sees a funeral procession, if he is not walking with it, let him stand until he leaves it behind, or it leaves him behind, or it is put down before it leaves him behind.”

comparisons.note: Names Amr rather than Amir ibn Rabiah. Both he-leaves-it-behind and it-leaves-him-behind remain. Ibn Hajar identifies the first or as transmission uncertainty; do not collapse it to one direction.

segments.arabic: [1247] حدثنا أحمد بن يونس حدثنا ابن أبي ذئب عن سعيد المقبري عن أبيه قال
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: كنا في جنازة فأخذ أبو هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه بيد مروان فجلسا قبل أن توضع فجاء أبو سعيد رضى الله تعالى عنه فأخذ بيد مروان، فقال قم فوالله لقد علم هذا أن النبي ﷺ نهانا عن ذلك، فقال أبو هريرة صدق
segments.english: We were at a funeral. Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, took Marwan’s hand, and they sat down before it was put down. Abu Sa‘id, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, came and took Marwan’s hand, saying, “Stand up. By Allah, this man certainly knows that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade us from doing that.” Abu Hurayrah said, “He spoke the truth.”

comparisons.note: Adds Abu to Said al-Maqburi in the opening attribution.

segments.arabic: [1248] حدثنا مسلم يعني ابن إبراهيم حدثنا هشام حدثنا يحيى عن أبي سلمة عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ قال:

segments.arabic: [1249] حدثنا معاذ بن فضالة حدثنا هشام عن يحيى عن عبيد الله بن مقسم عن جابر بن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Miqsam, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: مرت بنا جنازة فقام لها النبي ﷺ وقمنا له فقلنا يا رسول الله إنها جنازة يهودي قال إذا رأيتم الجنازة فقوموا

comparisons.note: Renders the standing relation as with him, while the selected له and modern به differ; preserve and review the selected form.

checkedBody: Narrated Jabir bin 'Abdullah :

A funeral procession passed in front of us and the Prophet stood up and we too stood up. We said, 'O Allah's Apostle! This is the funeral procession of a Jew." He said, "Whenever you see a funeral procession, you should stand up."
comparisons.note: Does not explicitly retain the selected له relation in the shared standing phrase.

notes: The selected standing pronoun differs from both prints; preserve each reading explicitly for wording review.

The selected له is rendered because he did following Ibn Hajar’s explanation that it refers to standing because of the Prophet’s standing. The historical excerpt is explicitly corrected to فقمنا; the selected and modern readings remain unchanged.

segments.arabic: [1250] حدثنا آدم حدثنا شعبة حدثنا عمرو بن مرة قال: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى قال:
segments.english: Adam related to us: Shu‘bah related to us: ‘Amr ibn Murrah related to us; he said: I heard ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla say:

segments.arabic: كان سهل بن حنيف وقيس بن سعد قاعدين بالقادسية فمروا عليهما بجنازة فقاما فقيل لهما إنها من أهل الأرض
segments.english: Sahl ibn Hunayf and Qays ibn Sa‘d were sitting at al-Qadisiyyah. They passed them with a funeral procession, and the two stood. They were told, “It is one of the people of the land”—

segments.arabic: أي من أهل الذمة
segments.english: that is, one of the people of the covenant of protection—

segments.arabic: فقالا إن النبي ﷺ مرت به جنازة فقام فقيل له إنها جنازة يهودي، فقال أليست نفسا،
segments.english: and the two said, “A funeral procession passed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he stood. He was told, ‘It is the funeral of a Jew.’ He said, ‘Is it not a soul?’”

segments.arabic: وقال أبو حمزة عن الأعمش عن عمرو عن ابن أبي ليلى قال: كنت مع قيس وسهل رضى الله تعالى عنهما فقالا كنا مع النبي ﷺ،
segments.english: And Abu Hamzah said, from al-A‘mash, from ‘Amr, from Ibn Abi Layla, who said: I was with Qays and Sahl, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, and they said, “We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

segments.arabic: وقال زكريا عن الشعبي عن ابن أبي ليلى كان أبو مسعود وقيس يقومان للجنازة
segments.english: And Zakariyya said, from al-Sha‘bi, from Ibn Abi Layla: Abu Mas‘ud and Qays used to stand for the funeral procession.

comparisons.note: Retains closing statements but omits their Abu Hamzah/A’mash/Amr and Zakariyya/Sha’bi transmission routes.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Abdur Rahman bin Abi Laila:

Sahl bin Hunaif and Qais bin Sad were sitting in the city of Al-Qadisiya. A funeral procession passed in front of them and they stood up. They were told that funeral procession was of one of the inhabitants of the land i.e. of a non-believer, under the protection of Muslims. They said, "A funeral procession passed in front of the Prophet and he stood up. When he was told that it was the coffin of a Jew, he said, "Is it not a living being (soul)?"
comparisons.note: Omits both complete closing corroborating routes and their statements.

notes: One selected entry contains modern printed 1312/1313 plus full closing corroborations; the EPUB omits those endings.

segments.arabic: [1251] حدثنا عبد العزيز بن عبد الله حدثنا الليث عن سعيد المقبري عن أبيه أنه سمع أبا سعيد الخدري رضى الله تعالى عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us: Al-Layth related to us, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from his father, that he heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا وضعت الجنازة واحتملها الرجال على أعناقهم فإن كانت صالحة قالت قدموني وإن كانت غير صالحة قالت: يا ويلها أين يذهبون بها يسمع صوتها كل شيء إلا الإنسان ولو سمعه صعق
segments.english: “When the body is placed and men carry it on their necks, if it is righteous, it says, ‘Carry me forward.’ If it is not righteous, it says, ‘Woe to it! Where are they taking it?’ Everything hears its voice except the human being. If he heard it, he would faint.”

comparisons.note: Changes the third-person wording يا ويلها أين يذهبون بها to mixed first/second-person speech; review the pronoun ownership from the selected Arabic. The historical print has second-person تذهبون while selected and modern have third-person يذهبون. The English you therefore has a printed basis, but does not reproduce this selected occurrence; it is not evidence of an unequivocal error.

checkedBody: Narrated Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri :

Allah's Apostle said, When the funeral is ready and the men carry it on their shoulders, if the deceased was righteous it will say, 'Present me (hurriedly),' and if he was not righteous, it will say, 'Woe to it (me)! Where are they taking it (me)?' Its voice is heard by everything except man and if he heard it he would fall unconscious."
comparisons.note: Adds hurriedly and explanatory pronoun parentheses beyond the selected wording.

notes: The occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.

Keep one Carry-me-forward command, third-person woe and taking pronouns, Messenger-of-Allah attribution and fainting. No hurriedly, repeated command or to-its-people is imported. The historical second-person variant explains a comparison difference.

The historical wording asks where you are taking it; selected and modern ask where they are taking it. This is a printed variant, not an unequivocal error in an English comparison based on the other person. segments.arabic: [1252] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله حدثنا سفيان قال حفظناه من الزهري عن سعيد بن المسيب عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us: Sufyan related to us; he said: We memorized it from al-Zuhri, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: أسرعوا بالجنازة فإن تك صالحة فخير تقدمونها وإن يك سوى ذلك فشر تضعونه عن رقابكم
segments.english: “Carry the funeral quickly. If it is righteous, then it is a good thing you are bringing forward. If it is otherwise, then it is an evil thing you are taking off your necks.”

comparisons.note: Supplies an endpoint in the good-outcome clause although the selected occurrence lacks the modern print’s إليه.

checkedBody: Narrated Abu Huraira:
The Prophet said, "Hurry up with the dead body for if it was righteous, you are forwarding it to welfare; and if it was otherwise, then you are putting off an evil thing down your necks."
comparisons.note: Supplies an endpoint in the good-outcome clause absent from selected text; the modern print separately has إليه. The endpoint reading is supported by the modern print and by classical elliptical analyses. Its absence from the selected letters is an edition/translation limit, not proof of an unambiguous English error.

notes: The occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.

Preserve We-memorized-it-from-al-Zuhri and the selected elliptical good clause. segments.arabic: [1253] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف حدثنا الليث حدثنا سعيد عن أبيه أنه سمع أبا سعيد الخدري رضى الله تعالى عنه قال: كان النبي ﷺ يقول:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: Al-Layth related to us: Sa‘id related to us, from his father, that he heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say:

segments.arabic: إذا وضعت الجنازة فاحتملها الرجال على أعناقهم فإن كانت صالحة قالت قدموني وإن كانت غير صالحة قالت لأهلها يا ويلها أين يذهبون بها يسمع صوتها كل شيء إلا الإنسان ولو سمع الإنسان لصعق
segments.english: “When the body is placed and men then carry it on their necks, if it is righteous, it says, ‘Carry me forward.’ If it is not righteous, it says to its people, ‘Woe to it! Where are they taking it?’ Everything hears its voice except the human being. If the human being heard it, he would faint.”

comparisons.note: Changes the selected third-person woe/where-they-take-it wording to mixed first/second-person speech. The historical print has second-person تذهبون while selected and modern have third-person يذهبون. Preserve this edition distinction, and retain Prophet used-to-say rather than replacing it with Messenger said.

checkedBody: Narrated Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri

The Prophet said, "When a funeral is ready and the men carry the deceased on their necks (shoulders), if it was pious then it will say, 'Present me quickly', and if it was not pious, then it will say, 'Woe to it (me), where are they taking it (me)?' And its voice is heard by everything except mankind and if he heard it he would fall unconscious."
comparisons.note: Omits لأهلها and adds quickly.
